author: ojiudezue
title: Arrival engine ships as option B: start and welcome scene act now; stop and pause wait on the live ownership test
summary: The step 8 arrival engine (arrival music, welcome scene, departure pause) ships as v5.108.33 together with the MA twin fix and the NM boot-settle fix, in one restart. Start and scene act from day one. The 15-minute stop and the departure pause are built and active, but they act only while URA still owns the playback, and a natural track change ends ownership. They will rarely fire until a 5-minute live MA test with the operator sets the final ownership rule. v6.0.0 waits for that.
why: The open question was who owns playback after a start. Stopping or pausing music a person chose is the costly mistake; a song left playing is cheap. Context ownership is the conservative default: any write URA did not create ends it. Only a live test on the real players can show whether the device's own track-change updates carry fresh contexts. Shipping the start now delivers the visible charter goal (identity-driven arrivals) without guessing the stop rule. Bundling the boot-settle fix saves one restart, and the operator allows one restart a day while awake.
implications: Expect `wait_ended_not_ours` lines after track changes; that is the designed outcome, not a bug. The live test decides between keeping context ownership and a looser rule (for example, same media id). v6.0.0 is anchored to that release. PERSON-PROFILE-PREFERENCES-1 stays open through it (arc-cut on .33).
alternatives_considered: Option A: hold the whole engine until the live test (delays the arrival start for no safety gain). Ship with a looser ownership rule now (risks stopping music a person chose). Ship the boot-settle fix alone first (costs an extra restart).
revisit_trigger: After the live MA test, or if arrival logs show stop/pause never acting across a week of opted-in arrivals.
